steps.say: One piece of bowel slides inside its neighbour like a collapsing telescope, dragging its blood supply with it. It peaks in babies between three months and three years, often after a tummy virus.
steps.tx: One bowel slides inside its neighbour like a telescope. **Intussusception** (bowel telescoping) peaks from **3 months to 3 years** (three months to three years) with half (**50 percent**) under **1 year** (one year) and under a quarter (**25 percent**) after age **2** (two years), usually idiopathic at the lymphoid rich **ileocecal valve** (colon entry) after viral illness or rotavirus vaccine swells the **lymphoid hyperplasia** (gland patches). The dragged mesentery chokes first.

vis.alt: Anatomical illustration of ileocolic intussusception with compressed mesentery beside an ultrasound inset showing the target sign.
vis.caption: Ileocolic telescoping drags mesentery into the sheath, choking blood supply. Peak age is 3 months to 3 years. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Pain that storms then settles, screaming with legs pulled up, bloody mucus stools and a sausage shaped lump all point one way. Older children more often hide a dragging lump, usually the remnant pouch.
steps.tx: Pain that comes in storms with calm gaps defines it. Colicky pain with leg drawing and quiet intervals plus vomiting, **currant jelly stool** (bloody mucus stool) and a palpable mass define it, and **lead points** (dragging lumps) reach **12 percent** (twelve percent) in older children with **Meckel diverticulum** (remnant pouch) commonest alongside polyps, Henoch Schonlein bleeding and duplications. A sausage mass in the belly seals the bedside call.

steps.say: Sound waves spot the bowel rings before dye confirms anything. A clear ring pattern on scan skips straight to pressure treatment.
steps.tx: Sound waves spot the rings before dye confirms. **Ultrasound** (sound scan) **target sign** (bowel rings) in transverse view and **pseudokidney sign** (kidney shape) longitudinally trigger air or contrast enema, while plain film mass, sparse colonic gas or complete obstruction supports the diagnosis in half (**50 percent**) the cases. A clear target sign skips straight to reduction.

vis.alt: Ultrasound inset showing the target sign of intussusception in transverse view.
vis.caption: Target sign on transverse ultrasound with pseudokidney views lengthwise triggers enema reduction. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Pumped air usually unfolds what fingers cannot, succeeding in four of five cases. Many children go home the same day, and a repeat attempt hours later can still rescue failures.
steps.tx: Pressure usually fixes what fingers cannot. **Air enema** (pressure reduction) **reduction** (unfolding) succeeds above **80 percent** (eighty percent) with reflux into terminal ileum and mass resolution, many children discharge without admission, repeat enema hours later salvages some failures, and **recurrence** (returning telescope) is **11 percent** (eleven percent) usually within **24 hours** (twenty four hours). Watch one full day after success.

steps.say: An infected belly, an unstable child, a telescope beyond the colon or a third return all skip the enema queue. Surgeons unfold by pushing backward, and removal stays rare.
steps.tx: Four situations skip the enema queue. **Peritonitis** (infected belly), instability, purely small bowel location and **3rd** (third) recurrence form an **operative indication** (reason to open), reduction pushes proximally in retrograde fashion, resection stays rare so **ileocolectomy** (colon removal) is seldom needed, and post reduction fever resolves spontaneously. Open only these; the rest reduce by pressure.

steps.say: The commonest gut anomaly hides silently in one in fifty people as a true pouch from the yolk stalk. Stray stomach lining inside it explains the classic bleeding.
steps.tx: The commonest gut anomaly hides in 1 in 50 people. **Meckel diverticulum** (remnant pouch) is the commonest gut anomaly at **2 percent** (two percent), a true diverticulum from failed **vitelline duct** (yolk stalk) regression at **5 to 7 weeks** (five to seven weeks), with **heterotopic gastric mucosa** (stray stomach lining) in over **70 percent** (seventy percent) and pancreatic tissue in **5 percent** (five percent). Stray acid beside bowel bleeds.

steps.say: Twos unlock every exam question on this pouch: distance, length and age. The tracer scan lights up stomach lining but never pancreas tissue.
steps.tx: Twos unlock every exam question on this pouch. The **rule of twos** (twos memory aid) places it **2 feet** (two feet) from the valve at **2 inches** (two inches) long symptomatic by **2 years** (two years), and **technetium scan** (tracer camera) with **pertechnetate** (tracer chemical) detects gastric but never pancreatic mucosa. A bleeding scan that stays dark despite the classic story still goes to theatre.

steps.say: Painless floods in toddlers mean this pouch until proven otherwise. Bleeders lose the whole segment, quiet chance findings stay put, and non bleeders get a neat wedge.
steps.tx: Painless floods in toddlers mean this pouch until proven otherwise. **Lower GI bleeding** (bloody nappies) is painless and massive under **5 years** (five years) from the mesenteric sided ulcer opposite the diverticulum mouth, so **segmental resection** (segment removal) is gold standard while quiet V diverticulectomy with transverse closure suits nonbleeders, and an **incidental diverticulum** (chance finding) that is quiet is left alone. Resect bleeders, respect the quiet.
